title: Divided by discipline? A systematic literature review on the quantification of online sexism and misogyny using a semi-automated approach

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic literature review synthesizing natural language processing methods used to quantify, detect, and classify online sexism and misogyny, including an evaluation of how studies address algorithmic gender bias via data augmentation, regularization, and identity term replacement.

Reviewing existing literature on data annotation practices to assess how annotator demographics, domain expertise, and subjective interpretations impact inter-rater reliability and the resulting fairness of hate-speech detection models.

Analyzing the geographical and linguistic distribution of benchmark datasets in the literature, highlighting the over-representation of English/Western data and evaluating the limitations of translation and cross-lingual models for capturing cultural nuances.
